summary.headline: Kirloskar Ferrous Q4 FY26 PBT rose to INR514 crore from INR432 crore, with FY27 casting volume target of about 1.85 lakh tonnes.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 pig iron production fell 3% YoY to 1,58,152 tonnes after a roughly 3.5-month Hiriyur blast furnace stoppage cut FY26 output by about 68,000 tonnes. Casting volumes grew 13% in Q4 and 7% for the year, helped by Oliver Engineering in Rajpura, while tube production rose 6% in Q4. Management said pig iron prices recovered in Q4 and into April, with reported PBT of INR514 crore versus INR432 crore a year earlier. Management guided to 15% volume growth in FY27 and an EBITDA margin of about 12.5%, below its 15% comfort level.

financial_highlights.change: approx. INR 100 crore improvement on PBT per management

segments.name: Pig iron
segments.commentary: Q4 production 1,58,152 t (down 3% YoY); Q4 sales 1,27,600 t (down about 6% from 1,35,000 t). FY26 production 6,23,939 t vs 6,31,103 t; Hiriyur stoppage cost about 68,000 t.

segments.name: Castings (incl. Oliver)
segments.commentary: Q4 production 36,596 t (up 13%) and sales 34,980 t (up 9%). FY26 production 1,48,564 t (up about 7%); including Oliver, about 1.62 lakh t, with Oliver contributing about 23,000 t (16% of sales).

segments.name: Tubes
segments.commentary: Q4 production 56,119 t (up 6%) and sales 51,106 t (flat vs 51,500 t). FY26 production 2,16,914 t vs 1,99,443 t; FY26 sales 1,88,700 t vs 1,68,800 t.

segments.name: Steel
segments.commentary: Q4 production 58,119 t (down about 10%) and sales 24,812 t (up 20% from 20,700 t). FY26 production about 2.40 lakh t vs 2.42 lakh t, hit by two fume-extraction shutdowns.

segments.name: Oliver Engineering
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR 118-119 crore on about 17,000 t; FY27 target about 24,000-25,000 t and INR 240-250 crore. Monthly run rate was 1,700 t in Jan-Mar and about 1,800 t in April.

guidance_outlook: FY27 casting volume target about 1,85,000 t (management reiterated 1,80,000-1,90,000 t, production basis), with 2-3% foundry rejection causing a small gap to sales.
FY27 overall sales volume growth of at least 15%, conditional on commodity prices not falling again.
Tube volume growth of 10-11% targeted in FY27 via debottlenecking; management expects about half of the 10% realisation drop (5-6%) to be recovered.
EBITDA margin expected to be just above 12.5%; management comfortable only at 15%.
Solar and wind power: about 35 MW solar and 25 MW wind to be commissioned June-September 2026; FY27 benefit about INR 45 crore, rising to about INR 90 crore at full run-rate.
Capex of about INR 600-700 crore per year, including about INR 500 crore for a bigger-diameter tube mill at Baramati (completion in about 1.5 years).
Oliver merger into KFIL targeted within a couple of months, to count for FY26.
capex_capacity: Solapur foundry running at about 4,200 t/month against a 6,000 t/month minimum expectation (about 70% utilisation); target about 5,000 t/month and 55,000-56,000 t sales in FY27.
Oliver Rajpura run rate about 1,700 t/month in Jan-Mar; target 2,000 t/month average and 24,000-25,000 t in FY27.
Sixth large-casting foundry being commissioned; seventh foundry planning started. Long-term feasibility up to 3 lakh t/year castings.
Baramati seamless tube capacity to rise from 2.30 lakh t to 4 lakh t by adding 1.5 lakh t; 1.5-year project for bigger tube mill.
Hiriyur blast furnace upgrade for about INR 125-150 crore to 2.5-3 lakh t/year; Koppal oxygen plant of 150 t/day by year end, with oxygen enrichment to 5% from 2.5% and PCI to 160-170 kg from 130 kg.
Jambunath Gudda iron ore mines, beneficiation and pellet plant planned; 52 MW waste-heat power in operation; Jejuri at about 30% green power.
demand_pricing: Pig iron prices up INR 5,000/t vs October and INR 4,000/t vs December (per management); international pig iron at about $475/t. Q4 realisation lagged due to order-book lag and some spill into January, with further price correction in April.
Casting realisation about INR 125/kg in base; management expects it to go beyond INR 130/kg within two years, with INR 10-12/kg of commodity-linked reductions expected to partly flow back.
Three new casting customers added in Q4 (diesel engine maker, tractor and earthmoving exporters); export share rose from 20% to 28% and CV share from 12% to 16% (per analyst's figures).
Oliver machining value expected to reach about INR 100 crore within a year, with 22 HMCs installed.
Cost pressures: rupee at about INR 95/$ and coal up about $25/t, which management expects to be partly passed on.
Tube NSR about INR 1,13,000/t at FY26 end; management expects tube prices to rise in coming months.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 casting target of 1.85-1.9 lakh t still achievable given slower ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 1,80,000-1,90,000 t as target, with about 1.05 lakh t from Koppal, 60,000 t from Solapur and 25,000 t from Oliver; the 45,000 t/quarter run rate expected within a couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin trajectory and backward integration plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects just above 12.5% EBITDA, aims for 15% and cited coke self-sufficiency, 52 MW waste-heat power, Jambunath mines and pellet plant as backward integration steps.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 pig iron price hikes lag and how will Q1 FY27 spreads move?
qa_highlights.answer: Lag came from 15-day order books and monthly commitments to regular customers; price increase effect partly in April. Management said pig iron price increase is inevitable but coal and coke costs are rising, and it is still assessing spreads.

qa_highlights.question: How much power cost saving from solar, wind and captive power?
qa_highlights.answer: Solar delivered about INR 70 crore benefit in FY26; wind and solar commissioning June-September should add about INR 45 crore in FY27, with INR 90 crore possible at full run-rate after new Maharashtra regulations.

qa_highlights.question: Tube business order book and ONGC orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have the pending order figure; expects new tenders this year and better domestic and export oil and gas demand. Targets 10-11% volume growth in tubes.

qa_highlights.question: Tube capacity expansion and capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Bigger tube mill at Baramati about INR 500 crore, within a 1.5-year completion; total capex about INR 600-700 crore per year, with borrowings reduced.

risks_watch: Casting ramp-up at Solapur (about 70% utilisation) and foundry-process complexity could delay the 1.85 lakh t FY27 target.
Pig iron pricing recovery depends on realisation after cost increases in coal and coke and rupee at about INR 95/$.
Hiriyur blast furnace output and Koppal productivity gains (oxygen, PCI) need to show in Q1 FY27.
Solar and wind commissioning timing (June-September) and new Maharashtra regulations on green power utilisation.
Oil and gas tube orders (including ONGC) remain unconfirmed; management had no current order book figure.
summary.management_tone: Management was optimistic on pricing and volumes but cautious on execution, repeatedly flagging Solapur ramp-up as difficult and commodity prices as uncertain. Some answers were incomplete (the MD could not give the Q4 other-expense detail or the tube order book), and the sales-volume and realisation figures were quoted loosely and with corrections.
key_quotes: Our effort to grow 20%, 25% are not realistic.
I have been talking about that we are comfortable only when we are at 15% EBITDA.
I think we are committed to the numbers what you mentioned, 1,80,000, 1,85,000, 1,90,000 is the numbers we look forward.

adds.what: Baramati seamless tube capacity +1.5 lakh t/yr (2.30 to 4 lakh t) via bigger-diameter tube mill
Sixth large-casting foundry being commissioned (Solapur/Kirloskar casting)
Hiriyur blast furnace upgrade to 2.5-3 lakh t/yr

growth.why: Management guides at least 15% overall FY27 volume growth and 10-11% tube volume growth, backed by Solapur utilisation at ~70% (4,200 vs 6,000 t/month), a sixth foundry in trials, Oliver's run rate rising to 2,000 t/month, and 60 MW of renewables in Q2 FY27; the Baramati tube expansion is ~6 quarters out and EBITDA margin guided only just above 12.5%, below management's 15% comfort level.
